newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-LIERSE WIN BELGIAN TITLE FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1960.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIERSE WIN BELGIAN TITLE FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1960.

text.p: Lierse clinched their first Belgian league title since 1960 on Sunday with a 3-0 away win against Standard Liege.
Lierse took charge quickly with first-half goals from Dirk Huysmans, Eric Van Meir and David Brocken.
They finished the season two points clear of outgoing champions Club Brugge.
Based in Lier, a northern Belgian town of 33,000 inhabitants, Lierse sealed the title for the fourth time in their history with their first away victory over Standard Liege in 37 years.
The match was halted when Standard fans spilled on to the pitch eight minutes from time and refused to return to the stands. It was resumed nearly half an hour later.
Club Brugge beat Ghent 1-0 through a first-half penalty by Belgium midfielder Lorenzo Staelens but had effectively wasted their title chances last week when they were defeated by Antwerp.
Anderlecht secured a berth in next season's UEFA Cup by beating Mechelen 2-0 to leapfrog into fourth place over Lommel, who were held 3-3 by lowly Lokeren.
It will be the 35th successive appearance on the European stage for Anderlecht, who face Ekeren in the Belgian Cup final next Sunday.
Lommel will take the last UEFA Cup place if Anderlecht win the cup and contest next season's European Cup Winners' Cup.
Former European Cup Winners' Cup champions Mechelen and Cercle Brugge will be relegated and replaced by second division champions Beveren and the winners of a four-team play-off.
